intent.raw_query: Seoul K-culture and food, $2200 couple, winter from LAX

experiences.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Experience
experiences.description: Explore the iconic 14th-century Gyeongbokgung Palace while dressed in a traditional Hanbok robe. Many rental shops surrounding the palace offer affordable Hanbok rentals, and wearing one grants you free entry to the palace. Witness the ceremonial Changing of the Royal Guard and stroll through the grand courtyards for an immersive dive into Joseon Dynasty culture.

experiences.name: Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into Seoul's oldest and most beloved traditional market, famous for its vibrant food stalls. Sample iconic Korean street foods including bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap (mini seaweed rice rolls), tteokbokki (spicy rice cakes), and fresh yukhoe (beef tartare). Interact with local vendors and experience the authentic sights, sounds, and flavors of everyday Korean culinary life.

experiences.name: K-Pop Idol Dance Class
experiences.description: Learn choreography from your favorite K-Pop songs at one of Hongdae's many dedicated K-Pop dance academies. Professional instructors teach routines from groups like BTS, BLACKPINK, and NewJeans in a fun, energetic group setting. This is a quintessential K-culture experience that lets you live out your idol fantasies and connect with fellow K-Pop fans from around the world.

experiences.name: Insadong Cultural Village & Tea House Exploration
experiences.description: Wander through the charming alleyways of Insadong, Seoul's premier cultural district filled with traditional tea houses, antique shops, indie galleries, and Korean craft stores. Stop into a traditional Hanok-style tea house to enjoy a ceremonial cup of omija (five-flavor berry) or barley tea paired with Korean rice cakes. Explore Ssamziegil, a quirky open-air shopping complex showcasing local artisan goods and handmade crafts.

experiences.name: Authentic Korean BBQ Dinner Experience
experiences.description: Enjoy a classic Korean BBQ dinner at one of Mapo-gu's legendary charcoal grill restaurants, famous for their premium samgyeopsal (pork belly) and galbi (beef short ribs). Grill your own meat tableside, wrap it in fresh perilla leaves and lettuce, and pair it with an array of banchan (side dishes) and a glass of soju or makgeolli. This communal dining ritual is central to Korean social culture and an unmissable culinary highlight.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Seoul, South Korea
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Incheon International Airport at 22:30. Clear immigration and customs, then take the Airport Railroad Express (AREX) or bus to Bupyeong Station. Check in to Toyoko Inn Incheon Bupyeong. Pick up a T-money card at the airport convenience store for easy transit use throughout the trip.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport food court
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night snack at a 24-hour GS25 or CU convenience store near the hotel — try triangle kimbap, instant ramen, or a hot dog (under ₩5,000)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — just check in and rest. Exchange some cash at the airport for small purchases. Bupyeong is well-connected by subway (Line 1 & 7) making it a great budget base. Toyoko Inn typically includes a simple breakfast.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy the complimentary breakfast at Toyoko Inn. Then head to Bupyeong Modoo Mall and Bupyeong Underground Shopping Center — one of Korea's largest underground markets, great for affordable K-fashion, accessories, and street snacks. Browse and soak in local shopping culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take subway Line 1 to Incheon's Chinatown (Incheon Jung-gu). Walk through the colorful Chinatown gate, explore the murals, and stroll along the nearby Open Port Area with its historic Japanese and Chinese colonial architecture. Visit Jayu Park for a panoramic view of Incheon port — free entry.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward Bupyeong and explore the Bupyeong Rodeo Street area for evening street food and local vibes. Try tteokbokki, sundae (blood sausage), and hotteok from street stalls.

meals.breakfast: Complimentary breakfast at Toyoko Inn
meals.lunch: Incheon Chinatown jjajangmyeon (black bean noodles) — a local specialty, around ₩7,000–₩9,000 at a small local restaurant
meals.dinner: Bupyeong street food stalls — tteokbokki + sundae + eomuk (fish cake soup) combo for under ₩8,000

day_by_day.notes: Dress in warm layers — December highs are around 3°C. Incheon Chinatown is walkable and free to explore. Carry cash for street food vendors.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway into Seoul (Line 1 toward Seoul Station, about 40–50 min). Visit Gyeongbokgung Palace — the grandest of Seoul's Five Grand Palaces. Arrive early for the 10:00 Royal Guard Changing Ceremony. Entry is ₩3,000. Wear or rent a hanbok at the palace entrance for free entry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through Bukchon Hanok Village — a preserved neighborhood of traditional Korean hanok houses. Stroll the narrow alleys and enjoy the contrast of old and new Seoul. Then head to nearby Insadong for K-culture shopping: traditional crafts, calligraphy, and unique Korean souvenirs at budget-friendly prices.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Insadong's Ssamziegil courtyard for indie shops and street performances. Head to Gwangjang Market (short subway ride) for one of Seoul's most iconic street food experiences.

meals.breakfast: Complimentary breakfast at Toyoko Inn
meals.lunch: Insadong area — try a set meal at a traditional Korean restaurant (doenjang jjigae + rice + banchan) for ₩8,000–₩10,000
meals.dinner: Gwangjang Market — bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak kimbap, and yukhoe (beef tartare) from market stalls, budget ₩10,000–₩15,000 total

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung is closed on Tuesdays. Hanbok rental near the palace costs ₩10,000–₩15,000 for 2 hours but grants free palace entry. Gwangjang Market is open until late and is a must for food lovers.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Hongdae (Hongik University area) — the heart of Seoul's youth and K-culture scene. Explore the vibrant street art, murals, and indie shops. Visit the free Trick Eye Museum exterior murals and browse the quirky boutiques along the main street.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Sinchon and Ewha Womans University area for more affordable K-fashion shopping and café culture. Visit the stunning Ewha campus architecture (free). Then head to the Han River (Yeouido or Mangwon) for a winter riverside walk — beautiful even in December.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hongdae for the evening street busking performances (K-pop cover dancers and musicians often perform on weekends). Explore the night market and pick up affordable K-pop merchandise from street vendors.

meals.breakfast: Complimentary breakfast at Toyoko Inn
meals.lunch: Hongdae area — try a Korean BBQ lunch set (samgyeopsal) at a budget restaurant, around ₩10,000–₩12,000 per person
meals.dinner: Hongdae street food — Korean corn dogs, tteokbokki, and a cup of warm sikhye (rice punch) for under ₩10,000

day_by_day.notes: Hongdae is most lively on Friday evenings. The area is very walkable. Many K-pop idol agency buildings (JYP, etc.) are nearby for fans. Bring hand warmers for the Han River walk.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Namsan Seoul Tower (N Seoul Tower) — take the cable car up (₩9,500 round trip) or hike the Namsan trail for free. Enjoy panoramic winter views of Seoul. See the famous love lock fences. The tower observation deck costs ₩21,000 but the outdoor view is free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down Namsan to Myeongdong — Seoul's most famous shopping and street food district. Browse cosmetics shops (great deals on K-beauty products), and enjoy the dense concentration of street food stalls along the main street.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Myeongdong Night Market (runs until ~11 PM). Then visit nearby Namdaemun Market — one of Korea's oldest and largest traditional markets, great for budget shopping and local atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Complimentary breakfast at Toyoko Inn
meals.lunch: Myeongdong street food lunch — lobster grilled cheese, tornado potato, egg bread, and Korean fried chicken skewers, budget ₩10,000–₩15,000
meals.dinner: Namdaemun Market — galchi jorim (braised hairtail fish) or seolleongtang (ox bone soup) at a local pojangmacha (street tent restaurant) for ₩8,000–₩10,000

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is busy in Myeongdong — go early for the cable car to avoid queues. K-beauty products in Myeongdong are competitively priced; compare before buying. Namdaemun closes early on Sundays.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace and its famous Secret Garden (Huwon) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Guided tours of the Secret Garden run at set times (₩8,000 for the garden tour, ₩3,000 for the palace). Book in advance as spots are limited, especially on weekends.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Changgyeonggung Palace next door (₩1,000 entry) and then stroll through the connected Jongmyo Shrine — a UNESCO-listed Confucian royal shrine (₩1,000 entry). The serene, forested grounds are beautiful in winter.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) — a stunning futuristic building by Zaha Hadid, free to walk around outside. The surrounding Dongdaemun area comes alive at night with massive shopping malls and street vendors.

meals.breakfast: Complimentary breakfast at Toyoko Inn
meals.lunch: Near Jongmyo — try a local gukbap (rice soup) restaurant for a warming winter meal, around ₩7,000–₩9,000
meals.dinner: Dongdaemun area — visit a 24-hour pojangmacha for ramyeon, odeng, and makgeolli (rice wine) for under ₩12,000

day_by_day.notes: Changdeokgung Secret Garden tours are in Korean and English — check the schedule at the palace website. Jongmyo is closed on Tuesdays. DDP hosts rotating free exhibitions worth checking out.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Suwon — take subway Line 1 from Bupyeong directly to Suwon Station (about 1 hour, under ₩2,000). Visit Hwaseong Fortress — a UNESCO World Heritage fortress wall you can walk along for free (some sections have a small fee of ₩1,000). The winter scenery is stunning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Suwon's Haenggung Palace (₩1,500 entry) inside the fortress. Then visit the nearby Suwon Ipark Museum or simply walk the fortress perimeter — about 5.7 km total. Stop at the Paldalmun Gate area for photos.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Bupyeong/Incheon. Relax and explore the local neighborhood around the hotel. Visit a local jjimjilbang (Korean sauna/bathhouse) near Bupyeong for a budget-friendly cultural experience and to warm up.

meals.breakfast: Complimentary breakfast at Toyoko Inn
meals.lunch: Suwon galbi (short rib BBQ) — Suwon is famous for it. Try a budget lunch set near the fortress for ₩12,000–₩15,000
meals.dinner: Local Bupyeong restaurant — sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew) set meal for ₩8,000–₩9,000

day_by_day.notes: Suwon Hwaseong is one of Korea's best-preserved fortresses and very underrated. The jjimjilbang near Bupyeong costs around ₩8,000–₩12,000 and includes access to hot baths, saunas, and rest areas — great for budget travelers.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Itaewon and the adjacent Haebangchon (HBC) neighborhood — a multicultural area with a unique mix of Korean and international culture. Visit the War Memorial of Korea (free entry to the outdoor exhibits, ₩5,000 for indoor galleries) — one of Seoul's most impressive and moving museums.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Gyeongnidan-gil — a trendy street with independent cafés, vintage shops, and street art. Browse the unique boutiques and enjoy the neighborhood's creative atmosphere. Then head to nearby Yongsan Electronics Market if interested in tech gadgets and K-pop merchandise.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Banpo Bridge Rainbow Fountain area (the fountain runs seasonally — check if operating in December) or simply walk along the Han River at Banpo Hangang Park for a peaceful winter evening.

meals.breakfast: Complimentary breakfast at Toyoko Inn
meals.lunch: Itaewon area — try a Korean-style burger or a budget international meal (shawarma, etc.) for around ₩8,000–₩12,000
meals.dinner: Gyeongnidan-gil — find a cozy local Korean restaurant for kimchi jjigae (kimchi stew) set meal for ₩8,000–₩10,000

day_by_day.notes: The War Memorial of Korea is closed on Mondays. Gyeongnidan-gil is a great alternative to the more touristy Itaewon main street. Dress very warmly for any Han River evening walks.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Lotte World — one of the world's largest indoor theme parks in Jamsil. A full-day ticket costs around ₩62,000, but if budget is tight, the outdoor Magic Island area and the adjacent Lotte World Mall are free to explore. The nearby Seokchon Lake is beautiful in winter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk around Seokchon Lake (free) — a scenic lake surrounded by Lotte Tower and decorated with Christmas lights in December. Visit the Lotte World Tower Sky31 observation deck (₩27,000) for incredible city views, or admire the tower from outside for free.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Jamsil's Rodeo Street for evening shopping and street food. The area has many affordable Korean restaurants and trendy cafés.

meals.breakfast: Complimentary breakfast at Toyoko Inn
meals.lunch: Lotte World Mall food court — Korean bibimbap or a noodle dish for ₩8,000–₩10,000
meals.dinner: Jamsil area — try dakgalbi (spicy stir-fried chicken) at a local restaurant for ₩10,000–₩12,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: December is a festive time at Lotte World with Christmas decorations. If skipping the theme park, the lake walk and mall are completely free and very enjoyable. Check for any Christmas market events in the area.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Bukhansan National Park — Seoul's urban mountain park. Take the subway to Gupabal or Dobongsan station and hike one of the beginner-friendly trails. The winter scenery with snow-dusted granite peaks is spectacular. Free entry to the park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city and head to Sinchon or Hongdae for Christmas Eve shopping and festive atmosphere. Korean Christmas is celebrated as a romantic holiday — the streets are beautifully decorated.
day_by_day.evening: Experience a Korean Christmas Eve in Myeongdong or Hongdae — both areas have Christmas markets, street performances, and festive decorations. Join locals celebrating with street food and hot drinks.

meals.breakfast: Complimentary breakfast at Toyoko Inn
meals.lunch: Pack kimbap from a convenience store for the hike (under ₩3,000) or eat at a mountain trail snack stand
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve special — treat yourself to a slightly nicer Korean BBQ dinner in Hongdae, budget ₩15,000–₩20,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Bukhansan requires sturdy shoes with good grip — trails can be icy in December. Bring crampons or hiking poles if possible. Christmas Eve in Seoul is very lively — book dinner early if going to a restaurant.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple — the head temple of Korean Buddhism in central Seoul, free entry. The temple is beautifully decorated with lanterns year-round. Nearby Insadong is quieter on Christmas morning — a good time to browse without crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Seodaemun Prison History Hall (₩3,000) — a powerful and important historical site documenting Korea's independence movement during Japanese colonial rule. Then walk to nearby Gyeonghuigung Palace (free entry) — one of Seoul's lesser-visited palaces.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Cheonggyecheon Stream — a restored urban stream running through central Seoul, beautifully lit at night. Walk along the stream from Gwanghwamun toward Dongdaemun. Free and very scenic.

meals.breakfast: Complimentary breakfast at Toyoko Inn
meals.lunch: Insadong — traditional Korean set meal (hanjeongsik lite) at a local restaurant for ₩10,000–₩12,000
meals.dinner: Cheonggyecheon area — find a local pojangmacha for hot ramyeon and oden for under ₩10,000, or try a nearby gimbap restaurant

day_by_day.notes: Many shops may have reduced hours on Christmas Day. Jogyesa Temple and Cheonggyecheon are always open and free. The stream walk is about 5.8 km one way — you can walk part of it and take the subway back.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Korea in Yongsan — one of Asia's largest museums with an incredible collection of Korean artifacts spanning 5,000 years of history. Entry is FREE. Plan at least 2–3 hours here.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Gangnam district — made famous by PSY's song. Walk along Garosu-gil (tree-lined street) with its boutique shops and cafés. Visit the COEX Mall and its famous Starfield Library (free) — a stunning public library inside the mall. Browse the K-pop merchandise stores nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Gangnam's affordable local restaurants away from the main tourist strip. Then head back toward Bupyeong for a final evening at a local jjimjilbang or norebang (karaoke room) — a quintessential Korean cultural experience.

meals.breakfast: Complimentary breakfast at Toyoko Inn
meals.lunch: National Museum of Korea cafeteria — affordable Korean set meals for ₩7,000–₩9,000
meals.dinner: Gangnam back streets — try a local Korean restaurant for bulgogi (marinated beef) rice bowl for ₩9,000–₩12,000

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum of Korea is closed on Mondays. Starfield Library in COEX is free and very photogenic. Norebang rooms in Bupyeong cost around ₩10,000–₩15,000 per hour for a private room — great for groups.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy the complimentary breakfast at Toyoko Inn. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping at Bupyeong Underground Shopping Center or a nearby convenience store. Pick up Korean snacks, instant ramyeon, and K-beauty products to bring home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, visit a nearby local café for a final Korean coffee experience (Dalgona coffee or a traditional sikhye). Take a final walk around Bupyeong neighborhood to soak in the local atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Incheon International Airport via AREX or airport bus from Bupyeong. Allow at least 2–3 hours before departure for check-in and security. Grab a final Korean meal at the airport food court.

meals.breakfast: Complimentary breakfast at Toyoko Inn
meals.lunch: Local Bupyeong restaurant — final bowl of Korean comfort food: doenjang jjigae or kimchi jjigae set for ₩8,000
meals.dinner: Incheon Airport food court — bibimbap or Korean fried chicken for ₩10,000–₩13,000

day_by_day.notes: Check out time at Toyoko Inn is typically 11:00 AM — ask about luggage storage if your flight is later. The AREX from Bupyeong to the airport takes about 30–40 minutes. Duty-free shopping at Incheon Airport is excellent for last-minute K-beauty and snack purchases.

trip_options.title: Classic Seoul, South Korea Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Incheon International Airport at 22:30. Clear immigration and customs, collect baggage. Take Airport Railroad Express (AREX) or limousine bus to Bupyeong area. Check in to Toyoko Inn Incheon Bupyeong. Grab a late-night snack near the hotel at a nearby convenience store (GS25 or CU) or a 24-hour pojangmacha (street food tent).

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at airport
meals.dinner: Late-night convenience store snacks or instant ramen — try CU or GS25 near the hotel for Korean triangle kimbap, hotteok, or cup noodles (under ₩5,000)

day_by_day.notes: Wrap up early and rest well — long travel day. Pick up a T-money card at the airport or convenience store for easy transit use throughout the trip. Exchange some currency at the airport for better rates.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a hearty Korean breakfast near the hotel. Then head to Bupyeong Modoo Mall and Bupyeong Underground Shopping Center — one of Korea's largest underground markets, great for affordable K-fashion, accessories, and local goods. Explore the vibrant street culture of Bupyeong district.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the subway (Line 1) to Incheon Chinatown and Sinpo International Market. Walk through Korea's only Chinatown, admire the colorful murals and gates, then cross to Sinpo Market to try local Incheon specialties. Visit the nearby Jayu Park for a scenic winter stroll and views of Incheon port.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Bupyeong area. Explore the lively Bupyeong night market scene. Visit a local norebang (karaoke room) for a quintessential K-culture experience — rooms typically cost ₩15,000–25,000/hour per group.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby bakery — Paris Baguette or Tous Les Jours for coffee and pastries (₩5,000–8,000)
meals.lunch: Sinpo Market — try Sinpo-style dakgangjeong (sweet crispy chicken) and hotteok, Incheon's famous street foods (₩5,000–10,000)
meals.dinner: Bupyeong area Korean BBQ restaurant — samgyeopsal (pork belly) or galbi with banchan sides (₩15,000–20,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Dress in warm layers — December highs around 3°C. Bupyeong subway station (Line 1) connects easily to Incheon Chinatown (Incheon Station, 3 stops). T-money card makes transit seamless.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Seoul via subway (Line 1 from Bupyeong to Seoul Station, ~50 min). Head to Gyeongbokgung Palace — Korea's grandest Joseon-era palace. Arrive early for the 10:00 AM royal guard-changing ceremony at Gwanghwamun Gate. Explore the palace grounds and the beautiful Hyangwonjeong Pavilion, especially scenic in winter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the National Folk Museum of Korea inside the palace grounds (free with palace ticket). Then stroll through Bukchon Hanok Village — a preserved neighborhood of traditional Korean hanok houses with stunning views of the city. Browse local craft shops and galleries along the way.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Insadong for dinner and evening exploration. This cultural street is lined with traditional tea houses, art galleries, and K-culture shops. Visit Ssamziegil — a quirky open-air shopping complex with indie Korean brands and street performances.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or grab kimbap from a convenience store for the commute
meals.lunch: Insadong or Gyeongbokgung area — try a traditional Korean set meal (한정식 hanjeongsik lite) at a mid-range restaurant (₩12,000–18,000)
meals.dinner: Insadong — Tosokchon Samgyetang (ginseng chicken soup) nearby, or a cozy Korean restaurant in Insadong alley (₩12,000–20,000)

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung Palace entry: ₩3,000. Wearing hanbok (traditional dress) grants free entry — rental shops nearby charge ₩15,000–25,000/hour. Bukchon can be slippery in winter; wear sturdy shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace and its famous Secret Garden (Huwon) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Secret Garden tour (₩8,000) takes you through serene forested paths and traditional pavilions, magical in winter. Book in advance as tours are limited.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Jongno and Tapgol Park, then head to Cheonggyecheon Stream — a beautifully restored urban stream running through central Seoul. Walk along the lit stream path (especially lovely in the evening). Visit the nearby Gwangjang Market — one of Seoul's oldest and most authentic traditional markets.
day_by_day.evening: Stay at Gwangjang Market for dinner — this is a must for food lovers. The market comes alive at night with pojangmacha stalls. Explore the vibrant Friday night atmosphere in the Jongno area afterward.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or a local Korean breakfast spot — try haejang-guk (hangover soup) or doenjang jjigae (soybean paste stew) at a neighborhood restaurant (₩7,000–10,000)
meals.lunch: Gwangjang Market — bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak kimbap (mini kimbap), and yukhoe (beef tartare) — budget ₩10,000–15,000 for a full spread
meals.dinner: Gwangjang Market evening stalls — try eomuk (fish cake skewers), tteokbokki, and mandu (dumplings) with makgeolli (rice wine) (₩10,000–15,000)

day_by_day.notes: Changdeokgung entry: ₩3,000; Secret Garden tour: ₩8,000 — book online at the palace website. Gwangjang Market is cash-preferred. Cheonggyecheon Stream is beautifully lit at night — plan to walk it after dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Myeongdong — Seoul's most famous shopping and K-culture district. Explore the outdoor street market for K-beauty products, street food, and fashion. Visit the Myeongdong Cathedral, a stunning Gothic landmark. Browse flagship stores of Korean cosmetic brands like Innisfree, Etude House, and Olive Young.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the cable car up to N Seoul Tower (Namsan Tower) for panoramic views of Seoul in winter. Walk the Namsan Park trails (dress warmly). Visit the famous love lock fence and enjoy the city views from the observation deck.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Myeongdong for the vibrant Saturday night street food scene. The outdoor stalls are at their busiest on weekends. Explore the underground shopping malls and enjoy the festive December atmosphere with holiday decorations.

meals.breakfast: Myeongdong area — Korean-style breakfast at a local restaurant or bakery
meals.lunch: Myeongdong street food — try hotteok, tteokbokki, tornado potato, and Korean corn dogs (₩8,000–12,000 for a street food crawl)
meals.dinner: Myeongdong restaurant — Myeongdong Kyoja (famous for kalguksu knife-cut noodles and mandu) — very popular, expect a short wait (₩9,000–12,000)

day_by_day.notes: N Seoul Tower cable car: ₩9,500 round trip; observation deck: ₩16,000. Alternatively, hike up Namsan for free (30–40 min). Myeongdong is extremely busy on Saturdays — keep belongings secure.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) — a futuristic landmark designed by Zaha Hadid. Explore the design exhibitions and the surrounding Dongdaemun History & Culture Park. The area is especially photogenic in winter morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Hongdae (Hongik University area) — the heart of Seoul's youth culture, indie music, and street art. Explore the vibrant murals, independent boutiques, and K-pop culture shops. Visit the Trick Eye Museum or LINE Friends Store for fun K-culture experiences.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Hongdae for the Sunday evening busking performances — local musicians and dancers perform on the main street. Explore the club and bar scene or enjoy a relaxed evening at a themed café.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store — Sunday morning is quiet, grab supplies for the commute
meals.lunch: Hongdae area — try a trendy Korean fusion restaurant or a popular local spot like Yoogane (dakgalbi stir-fried chicken) (₩12,000–16,000)
meals.dinner: Hongdae — explore the restaurant alleys for Korean fried chicken and beer (chimaek) at a local chicken pub (₩15,000–22,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: DDP exhibitions vary — check the schedule at ddp.or.kr. Hongdae busking is weather-dependent in December but often continues even in cold weather. Trick Eye Museum entry: ₩15,000.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress — a UNESCO World Heritage Site about 1 hour from Bupyeong by subway. Walk the impressive fortress walls that encircle the city. Visit Hwaseong Haenggung Palace within the fortress grounds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Suwon's traditional market area near the fortress. Visit the Korean Folk Village nearby (30 min by bus) — a living museum of traditional Korean culture with folk performances, traditional crafts, and period architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Bupyeong/Incheon area. Enjoy a relaxed evening near the hotel — explore local restaurants and rest after a full day of walking.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before early departure
meals.lunch: Suwon — try Suwon galbi (Suwon-style short ribs), the city's most famous dish, at a local restaurant near the fortress (₩15,000–25,000)
meals.dinner: Back in Bupyeong — local Korean restaurant or a comforting bowl of sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew) at a neighborhood spot (₩8,000–12,000)

day_by_day.notes: Hwaseong Fortress entry: ₩1,000. Korean Folk Village entry: ₩15,000–25,000 depending on season. Check performance schedules in advance. Subway: Bupyeong → Suwon (Line 1, ~55 min, ₩1,850).

day_by_day.morning: Visit Lotte World — one of the world's largest indoor theme parks, perfect for a cold December day. Enjoy K-culture themed rides, the indoor ice skating rink, and the adjacent Lotte World Mall. The Magic Island outdoor section offers great views of Seokchon Lake.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Lotte World or head to nearby Seokchon Lake for a winter walk — the lake area is beautifully decorated for the holiday season. Visit the Songpa Naru Park area for local atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the COEX Mall in Gangnam — visit the famous Starfield Library (a stunning public library inside the mall), browse the aquarium, and enjoy the upscale shopping and dining options in the Gangnam district.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or grab breakfast near Jamsil station
meals.lunch: Lotte World food court — Korean bibimbap, bulgogi, or Korean fried chicken (₩10,000–15,000)
meals.dinner: COEX area — try a mid-range Korean restaurant in the mall or nearby Apgujeong/Gangnam streets (₩15,000–22,000)

day_by_day.notes: Lotte World admission: ₩62,000 for a full day pass (book online for discounts). COEX Aquarium: ₩29,000 if interested. Starfield Library is free. Gangnam is upscale — budget slightly more for dinner here.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Bukhansan National Park — Seoul's stunning mountain park offering winter hiking trails. Take the Bukhansanseong trail to see the ancient fortress walls and enjoy panoramic views of Seoul blanketed in winter. The Dobongsan area is also excellent for scenic winter hikes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend and head to the charming Seochon Village (west of Gyeongbokgung) — a quieter, more local alternative to Bukchon. Explore the narrow alleys, independent cafés, art galleries, and traditional hanok architecture. Visit the Gyeonghuigung Palace ruins nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Gwanghwamun Square for the Christmas/winter illuminations — the square is beautifully decorated in December. Enjoy the festive atmosphere and take evening photos of the lit-up Gyeongbokgung Gate.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before hiking
meals.lunch: Pack a convenience store lunch for the hike, or eat at a restaurant near the park entrance — dosirak (Korean lunchbox) style (₩8,000–12,000)
meals.dinner: Seochon or Gwanghwamun area — try a traditional Korean restaurant for a warming dinner like galbitang (short rib soup) or budae jjigae (army stew) (₩12,000–18,000)

day_by_day.notes: Bukhansan National Park is free to enter. Wear proper hiking boots and warm layers — trails can be icy in December. Crampons (아이젠) can be rented near the trailhead for ₩3,000–5,000. Start hiking early.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the War Memorial of Korea in Yongsan — a powerful and comprehensive museum covering Korean history and the Korean War. The outdoor exhibits include tanks, aircraft, and artillery. Free admission makes this excellent value.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Itaewon — Seoul's most international neighborhood. Explore the diverse restaurants, boutique shops, and the vibrant multicultural atmosphere. Visit Haebangchon (HBC) — a charming hillside neighborhood with indie cafés and great city views.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve in Seoul is a major celebration! Head to Myeongdong Cathedral for the Christmas Eve mass (open to all visitors) — a beautiful cultural experience. Enjoy the festive street atmosphere in Myeongdong with holiday lights, carolers, and special street food stalls.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or a local café near Yongsan
meals.lunch: Itaewon — explore the diverse food scene: try a Korean-fusion restaurant or international cuisine (₩12,000–20,000)
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve special — treat yourself to a slightly nicer Korean restaurant in Myeongdong or Itaewon for a festive dinner (₩20,000–35,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: War Memorial of Korea: free admission, closed Mondays. Christmas Eve is extremely busy in Myeongdong — arrive early for dinner reservations. The cathedral mass is a unique cultural experience regardless of religious background.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Day in Korea is a public holiday. Visit Jogyesa Temple — the head temple of Korean Buddhism in central Seoul. The temple is beautifully decorated with lanterns year-round and offers a peaceful contrast to the Christmas festivities. Attend a morning ceremony if interested.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Samcheong-dong area — a charming neighborhood of galleries, design shops, and cafés connecting Gyeongbokgung to Bukchon. Visit the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art (MMCA) Seoul branch for Korean contemporary art.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Banpo Bridge for the Moonlight Rainbow Fountain show (check seasonal schedule) or enjoy the Han River Park area. Many Koreans celebrate Christmas evening with friends — join the festive atmosphere in Hongdae or Sinchon.

meals.breakfast: Hotel — enjoy a relaxed Christmas morning breakfast
meals.lunch: Samcheong-dong café or restaurant — try a cozy Korean lunch set (₩12,000–18,000)
meals.dinner: Hongdae or Sinchon — Korean fried chicken and beer (chimaek) is a popular Korean Christmas tradition! (₩15,000–22,000)

day_by_day.notes: Some attractions may have modified hours on Christmas Day — check in advance. MMCA entry: ₩4,000. Jogyesa Temple is free. Chimaek (chicken + beer) on Christmas is a beloved Korean cultural tradition — embrace it!

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Korea in Yongsan — one of Asia's largest museums with an incredible collection of Korean artifacts spanning thousands of years. Free admission. Allow 2–3 hours to explore the highlights including the Goryeo celadon collection and ancient Buddhist art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Mangwon Market — a local neighborhood market beloved by Seoulites (less touristy than Gwangjang). Browse fresh produce, street food, and local goods. Then explore the trendy Mangwon and Hapjeong neighborhoods along the Han River — great for café hopping and local culture.
day_by_day.evening: Final big evening in Seoul — head to the 63 Building Observatory or Lotte World Tower Sky Observatory for stunning night views of Seoul. Then enjoy a farewell Korean BBQ dinner at a quality restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or local bakery
meals.lunch: Mangwon Market — try tteokbokki, sundae (Korean blood sausage), and hotteok (₩8,000–12,000)
meals.dinner: Farewell Korean BBQ — choose a well-reviewed samgyeopsal or chadolbaegi (beef brisket) restaurant in Hapjeong or Mapo area (₩18,000–25,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: National Museum of Korea: free, closed Mondays. Lotte World Tower Sky Observatory: ₩27,000. 63 Building Observatory: ₩16,000. Book dinner reservations in advance for Saturday evening. This is a great day for last-minute souvenir shopping.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy a leisurely breakfast near the hotel. Do any last-minute shopping at Bupyeong Underground Shopping Center for affordable souvenirs, K-beauty products, and snacks to bring home. Pack and check out of the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Incheon International Airport with plenty of time (allow 2–3 hours before departure). Browse duty-free shops at the airport for last-minute Korean snacks, cosmetics, and gifts. Enjoy a final Korean meal at the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a final Korean breakfast at a local restaurant near Bupyeong — try a warm bowl of seolleongtang (ox bone soup) for a hearty send-off (₩10,000–13,000)
meals.lunch: Incheon Airport food court or restaurants — try bibimbap or dosirak for a final Korean meal (₩12,000–18,000)
meals.dinner: On the plane or at airport depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Check airport transfer time carefully — from Bupyeong to Incheon Airport via AREX takes approximately 40–50 minutes. Allow extra time on Sunday. Keep some Korean won for last-minute purchases; exchange remaining currency at the airport. Duty-free allowances apply for items purchased.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Seoul, South Korea Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Experience
experiences.description: Explore the iconic 14th-century Gyeongbokgung Palace while dressed in a traditional Hanbok robe. Many rental shops surrounding the palace offer affordable Hanbok rentals, and wearing one grants you free entry to the palace. Witness the ceremonial Changing of the Royal Guard and stroll through the grand courtyards for an immersive dive into Joseon Dynasty culture.

experiences.name: Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into Seoul's oldest and most beloved traditional market, famous for its vibrant food stalls. Sample iconic Korean street foods including bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap (mini seaweed rice rolls), tteokbokki (spicy rice cakes), and fresh yukhoe (beef tartare). Interact with local vendors and experience the authentic sights, sounds, and flavors of everyday Korean culinary life.

experiences.name: K-Pop Idol Dance Class
experiences.description: Learn choreography from your favorite K-Pop songs at one of Hongdae's many dedicated K-Pop dance academies. Professional instructors teach routines from groups like BTS, BLACKPINK, and NewJeans in a fun, energetic group setting. This is a quintessential K-culture experience that lets you live out your idol fantasies and connect with fellow K-Pop fans from around the world.

experiences.name: Insadong Cultural Village & Tea House Exploration
experiences.description: Wander through the charming alleyways of Insadong, Seoul's premier cultural district filled with traditional tea houses, antique shops, indie galleries, and Korean craft stores. Stop into a traditional Hanok-style tea house to enjoy a ceremonial cup of omija (five-flavor berry) or barley tea paired with Korean rice cakes. Explore Ssamziegil, a quirky open-air shopping complex showcasing local artisan goods and handmade crafts.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Incheon International Airport at 22:30 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: No afternoon activities — flight is late evening
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Incheon Airport at 22:30. Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, and arrange private airport transfer to Toyoko Inn Incheon Bupyeong. Check in, freshen up, and settle into the hotel. Light late-night snack near the hotel if hungry.

meals.breakfast: On the flight
meals.lunch: On the flight or at the airport
meals.dinner: Late-night convenience store snack or 24-hour ramen shop near Bupyeong station (Bupyeong is known for its night food scene)

day_by_day.notes: Arrival is late at night — prioritize rest. Confirm hotel check-in arrangements in advance. Keep luggage light for easy transit. Exchange some KRW at the airport for convenience.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely hotel breakfast and orientation. Take the subway from Bupyeong station into central Seoul (approx. 40–50 min to central areas). Begin with a visit to Bukchon Hanok Village — stroll through the beautifully preserved traditional Korean hanok houses with panoramic views of the city. Dress warmly as temperatures will be around 3°C.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to nearby Insadong Cultural Village & Tea House Exploration — wander through charming alleyways lined with traditional craft shops, galleries, and antique stores. Stop into a premium traditional tea house such as Dawon (inside Unhyeongung Palace) for a ceremonial tea experience with Korean rice cakes.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Insadong or Jongno area. Explore the beautifully lit Cheonggyecheon Stream for a romantic winter evening walk before heading back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby café in Bupyeong
meals.lunch: Traditional Korean set meal (한정식) at Sanchon in Insadong — a renowned temple food restaurant offering multi-course vegetarian Korean cuisine
meals.dinner: Jungsik Seoul (2 Michelin stars) in Gwanghwamun area — modern Korean fine dining with seasonal tasting menus

day_by_day.notes: Layer up with thermal wear — December temperatures hover around 3°C. Bukchon Hanok Village is best visited in the morning before crowds arrive. Book Jungsik well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Experience — arrive early (9:00 AM) to rent a premium Hanbok from a nearby rental shop such as Hanboknam or Gyeongbokgung Hanbok. Explore the iconic 14th-century palace grounds in full traditional dress, including the National Folk Museum of Korea within the palace complex. Enjoy complimentary palace entry while wearing Hanbok.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Gyeonghuigung Palace or visit the National Palace Museum of Korea for deeper cultural immersion. Then head to Samcheong-dong for boutique shopping, art galleries, and café hopping along the charming tree-lined street.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Gwanghwamun Square to see the illuminated Admiral Yi Sun-sin statue and seasonal winter decorations. Enjoy a premium Korean BBQ dinner in the Jongno area.

meals.breakfast: Café Bora in Insadong or a hotel café — known for its matcha and traditional Korean-inspired pastries
meals.lunch: Tosokchon Samgyetang near Gyeongbokgung — famous for its premium ginseng chicken soup, perfect for warming up in winter
meals.dinner: Maple Tree House in Itaewon — upscale Korean BBQ with premium Hanwoo beef in a sophisticated setting

day_by_day.notes: Book Hanbok rental in advance for the best selection. The palace grounds are stunning in winter with occasional snow. Wear warm layers under the Hanbok. Gyeongbokgung opens at 9:00 AM.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace and its famous Secret Garden (Huwon) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The winter landscape of the Secret Garden is breathtaking with frost-covered pavilions and frozen ponds. Guided tours of the Secret Garden run at specific times; book in advance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the adjacent Changgyeonggung Palace and then make your way to the Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) — Zaha Hadid's futuristic landmark. Browse the design exhibitions and the surrounding Dongdaemun fashion district.
day_by_day.evening: Experience the vibrant Dongdaemun night market area. Visit the rooftop of DDP for city views, then enjoy a premium dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Anthracite Coffee Roasters in Huam-dong — specialty coffee in a converted factory space with artisan pastries
meals.lunch: Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour — dive into Seoul's oldest traditional market for bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap, and yukhoe (beef tartare) with a premium guided food tour
meals.dinner: Mingles in Cheongdam-dong (1 Michelin star) — innovative Korean cuisine blending traditional and modern techniques

day_by_day.notes: Secret Garden tours are limited — book online at the Changdeokgung website well in advance. The DDP is free to enter and open late. Gwangjang Market is best experienced with a local guide for the full food tour.

day_by_day.morning: Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour (Saturday is ideal for the market's full energy) — join a premium guided street food tour through Seoul's oldest and most beloved traditional market. Sample bindaetteok, tteokbokki, sundae, and fresh raw fish with expert commentary on Korean culinary history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Lotte World Tower and Sky Observatory (123 floors) for panoramic winter views of Seoul. Explore the Lotte World Mall for luxury shopping — home to flagship stores of major Korean and international luxury brands.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the trendy Seongsu-dong district — Seoul's 'Brooklyn' — for artisan coffee shops, concept stores, and creative spaces. Enjoy a premium dinner in this hip neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Paris Baguette premium café near Bupyeong
meals.lunch: Gwangjang Market food stalls — bindaetteok, mayak gimbap, and makgeolli (Korean rice wine) as part of the food tour
meals.dinner: Dosa in Seongsu-dong — a celebrated modern Korean restaurant with a creative seasonal menu in an industrial-chic setting

day_by_day.notes: Gwangjang Market is busiest on weekends — arrive with the tour group for the best experience and to avoid getting lost. Lotte Sky Observatory tickets should be booked online. Dress warmly for the outdoor market.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Namsangol Hanok Village — a beautifully restored traditional village at the foot of Namsan Mountain. Explore the five restored hanok houses, traditional performances, and cultural exhibits. Then take the Namsan Cable Car up to N Seoul Tower for stunning winter panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from Namsan and explore the upscale Myeongdong shopping district — browse Korean beauty flagship stores (Sulwhasoo, Innisfree, Amorepacific), international luxury brands, and street food stalls. Visit the Myeongdong Cathedral, a stunning Gothic landmark.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Gangnam district for an evening of luxury. Stroll through Apgujeong Rodeo Street and Cheongdam-dong luxury fashion district.

meals.breakfast: Café de Paris in Myeongdong or a hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Hadongkwan in Myeongdong — one of Seoul's most historic restaurants, famous for its premium gomtang (beef bone soup) since 1939
meals.dinner: Gaon in Gangnam (3 Michelin stars) — the pinnacle of Korean fine dining with an exquisite multi-course traditional Korean tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: Book Gaon restaurant well in advance — it is one of the hardest reservations to secure in Seoul. N Seoul Tower is magical at night with the love lock fence illuminated. Myeongdong is very crowded on Sundays.

day_by_day.morning: K-Pop Idol Dance Class in Hongdae — head to one of Hongdae's premier K-Pop dance academies (such as 1MILLION Dance Studio or Prepix Dance Academy) for a 2-hour group K-Pop choreography class. Learn moves from popular idol groups in a fun, energetic environment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Hongdae's vibrant street culture — browse independent music shops, K-Pop merchandise stores, and street art. Visit the Trick Eye Museum or the LINE Friends flagship store for interactive K-culture experiences.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Hongdae for the evening entertainment scene — live busking performances, neon-lit streets, and K-Pop themed cafés. Experience a premium Korean fried chicken and craft beer pairing at a top Hongdae restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Fritz Coffee Company in Mapo-gu — one of Seoul's most acclaimed specialty coffee roasters with excellent pastries
meals.lunch: Yeonnam-dong neighborhood near Hongdae — try Yeonnam Jang for premium Korean home-style cooking in a cozy setting
meals.dinner: Hongdae Dakgalbi — premium spicy stir-fried chicken with rice cakes, or visit Gopchang Jeongol for a luxurious beef intestine hot pot experience unique to Korean cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Book the K-Pop dance class in advance as popular sessions fill up quickly. 1MILLION Dance Studio offers classes in English. Wear comfortable athletic clothing for the dance class. Hongdae is most vibrant in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art — one of Asia's premier private art museums featuring an extraordinary collection of Korean traditional art alongside contemporary international works. The building itself, designed by three world-renowned architects, is a masterpiece.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Itaewon and the Haebangchon (HBC) neighborhood — Seoul's most international district with a fascinating mix of cultures. Visit the War Memorial of Korea for a deeply moving and comprehensive museum experience covering Korean history.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a premium spa and wellness experience at one of Seoul's luxury jjimjilbang (Korean bathhouse) — Dragon Hill Spa in Yongsan offers a premium multi-floor experience with various themed saunas, hot pools, and relaxation areas.

meals.breakfast: Tartine in Itaewon — a beloved artisan bakery with premium sourdough and pastries
meals.lunch: Vatos Urban Tacos in Itaewon — a Seoul institution blending Korean and Mexican flavors with premium ingredients
meals.dinner: Balwoo Gongyang near Jogyesa Temple — a Michelin-starred temple food restaurant offering an extraordinary multi-course Buddhist vegetarian meal

day_by_day.notes: Leeum Museum may have temporary exhibitions — check the schedule in advance. Dragon Hill Spa is open 24 hours and is a quintessential Korean cultural experience. Bring a change of comfortable clothes for the jjimjilbang.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress — a UNESCO World Heritage Site just 30 minutes from Seoul by subway. Walk the 5.7km fortress walls surrounding the old city, visit the Hwaseong Haenggung Palace, and explore the traditional Suwon Jidong Market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Suwon — visit the Korean Folk Village (Minsokchon) nearby for an immersive living museum of traditional Korean life with performances, craftspeople, and seasonal winter activities.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul and head to the Gangnam area for a sophisticated evening. Visit COEX Mall's famous Starfield Library for a stunning architectural experience before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before the early departure
meals.lunch: Suwon Galbi (Suwon-style short ribs) at Yeongdong Galbi in Suwon — this city is the birthplace of this iconic Korean BBQ dish
meals.dinner: Mosu Seoul in Gangnam (2 Michelin stars) — a celebrated tasting menu restaurant with a focus on seasonal Korean ingredients and French techniques

day_by_day.notes: Suwon Hwaseong Fortress is beautiful in winter, especially if there is snow. Wear very warm footwear as the fortress walls can be icy. The Korean Folk Village has special winter programs in December. Allow 3–4 hours for the full fortress walk.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple — the head temple of Korean Buddhism in central Seoul, beautifully decorated with thousands of lanterns for the winter season. Participate in a morning temple stay program or simply explore the serene grounds. Then visit the nearby Unhyeongung Palace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the upscale Cheongdam-dong and Apgujeong area for luxury shopping and gallery hopping. Visit the Amorepacific Museum of Art and browse the flagship stores of Korean luxury brands. Explore the Dosan Park area for premium boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve special dinner — Seoul transforms beautifully for Christmas with elaborate decorations throughout the city. Enjoy a premium Christmas Eve dinner at one of Seoul's top hotels or fine dining establishments.

meals.breakfast: Café Onion in Anguk — a beautifully restored hanok café with artisan coffee and Korean-inspired pastries
meals.lunch: Kwon Sooksoo in Cheongdam-dong — a celebrated Korean fine dining restaurant known for its artistic presentation of traditional Korean cuisine
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve special dinner at La Yeon in The Shilla Hotel (3 Michelin stars) — the ultimate Korean fine dining experience with a special holiday tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: Book La Yeon Christmas Eve dinner months in advance — it is one of the most sought-after reservations in Seoul. Jogyesa Temple is particularly beautiful in the evening with lantern illuminations. Seoul's Christmas decorations are spectacular — plan an evening stroll through Myeongdong.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas morning at leisure — enjoy a luxurious hotel breakfast. Take a peaceful winter walk along the Han River (Banpo Hangang Park) to enjoy the crisp morning air and city skyline views. The Banpo Bridge Rainbow Fountain is a Seoul landmark.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Korea — one of the largest museums in Asia with an extraordinary collection of Korean art and artifacts spanning 5,000 years of history. The museum is free to enter and world-class in its presentation.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas evening in Gangnam — visit the COEX area for festive decorations and atmosphere. Enjoy a premium Christmas dinner followed by a visit to a rooftop bar for cocktails with city views.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast or brunch at a premium hotel restaurant
meals.lunch: Noryangjin Fish Market — visit Seoul's famous wholesale fish market for an extraordinary fresh seafood lunch. Choose your live seafood and have it prepared on-site
meals.dinner: Ryunique in Gangnam — a creative fine dining restaurant with a unique tasting menu blending Korean and international influences, perfect for a special Christmas dinner

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Day in Seoul is a public holiday — most attractions and restaurants are open. The Han River is beautiful in winter but very cold — dress in full winter gear. Noryangjin Fish Market is open early morning; the lunch visit allows you to see it in full swing.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the vibrant Namdaemun Market — Korea's largest traditional market, a fascinating contrast to the luxury experiences of the trip. Explore the maze of stalls selling everything from traditional Korean goods to street food. Then visit nearby Deoksugung Palace with its famous stone wall road (Deoksugung Doldam-gil).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Seoul Museum of History for a comprehensive overview of Seoul's transformation from ancient capital to modern metropolis. Then explore the trendy Euljiro underground art district — a fascinating area of old printing shops converted into creative spaces and hip bars.
day_by_day.evening: Final premium shopping experience — visit the Lotte Department Store or Shinsegae Department Store flagship in central Seoul for last-minute luxury purchases and Korean beauty products. Enjoy a farewell dinner in a memorable setting.

meals.breakfast: Namdaemun Market street food — hotteok (sweet pancakes), tteokbokki, and odeng (fish cake soup) for an authentic market breakfast experience
meals.lunch: Myeongdong Kyoja — a Seoul institution famous for its premium kalguksu (knife-cut noodle soup) and mandu (dumplings), beloved by locals for decades
meals.dinner: Joo Ok in Jongno (1 Michelin star) — an intimate and sophisticated Korean fine dining experience with a focus on seasonal ingredients and traditional techniques

day_by_day.notes: Namdaemun Market is busiest on Saturday mornings — arrive early for the best experience. Deoksugung Palace has a famous changing of the guard ceremony at 11:00 AM and 2:00 PM. The Euljiro area is best explored in the evening when the creative bars and spaces come alive.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Seoul — enjoy a leisurely breakfast and last-minute packing. Take a final stroll through the Bupyeong area near the hotel to pick up any last souvenirs from the local market. Visit a nearby café for a final Korean coffee experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, visit the Incheon Chinatown and Jayu Park in nearby Incheon — a unique cultural enclave just minutes from the hotel with colorful murals, Chinese-Korean fusion food, and historic significance as Korea's first modern park.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Incheon International Airport. Allow ample time for check-in and the world-class airport experience — Incheon Airport has premium lounges, duty-free luxury shopping, a transit hotel, and cultural exhibitions. Depart Seoul with extraordinary memories.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or a premium café near Bupyeong station
meals.lunch: Incheon Chinatown — try jajangmyeon (black bean noodles) at Gonghwachun, the restaurant credited with introducing this iconic dish to Korea, or premium Chinese-Korean fusion at a top Chinatown restaurant
meals.dinner: Incheon Airport premium dining or airport lounge — Incheon has excellent dining options including Korean BBQ, sushi, and international cuisine in the departure terminal

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure flight details and allow at least 3 hours before international departure for Incheon Airport check-in. The airport's duty-free shops offer excellent deals on Korean beauty products, ginseng, and luxury goods. Consider purchasing premium Korean teas, traditional crafts, or Hanwoo beef jerky as final souvenirs.

query: Seoul K-culture and food, $2200 couple, winter from LAX
